tasks.description: Develop the backend to manage user data, including profile updates and activity tracking.

tasks.name: Implement Leaderboard Backend
tasks.description: Develop the backend logic to calculate and update user rankings for the leaderboard.

tasks.description: Create the frontend interface to display hints and explanations for problems.

tasks.name: Implement Hints and Explanations Backend
tasks.description: Develop the backend to manage hints and explanations for problems.

tasks.description: Perform testing to ensure the problem library works as expected.

tasks.name: Test Code Submission and Evaluation
tasks.description: Perform testing to ensure code submission and evaluation works correctly.

tasks.name: Test User Profiles
tasks.description: Perform testing to ensure user profiles are displayed and updated correctly.

tasks.name: Test Leaderboard Functionality
tasks.description: Perform testing to ensure the leaderboard displays accurate rankings.

tasks.name: Test Hints and Explanations
tasks.description: Perform testing to ensure hints and explanations are displayed correctly.

tasks.name: Deploy Problem-Solving Platform
tasks.description: Deploy the platform to a production environment.

T1.implementation_approach: Use a component-based design approach to create a responsive and user-friendly interface for browsing, searching, and filtering problems.
T1.notes: Focus on intuitive navigation and accessibility.

T2.implementation_approach: Develop RESTful APIs to handle problem creation, retrieval, updating, and deletion.
T2.notes: Ensure proper validation and error handling.

T3.implementation_approach: Design a schema to store problem details, including title, description, tags, difficulty, and test cases.

T4.implementation_approach: Create a form-based interface for users to write and submit code, with syntax highlighting and error feedback.
T4.notes: Include real-time feedback and auto-save functionality.

T5.implementation_approach: Set up a secure sandbox environment to execute user-submitted code and compare outputs with expected results.
T5.notes: Ensure security and prevent malicious code execution.

T6.implementation_approach: Design a profile page to display user details, activity history, and achievements.
T6.notes: Include editable fields for user information.

T7.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage user profiles, including retrieval and updates.

T8.implementation_approach: Create a leaderboard interface to display top users based on performance metrics.
T8.notes: Allow sorting and filtering by different criteria.

T9.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to calculate and retrieve leaderboard data based on user performance.

T10.implementation_approach: Design an interface to display hints and explanations for problems, with collapsible sections.
T10.notes: Ensure hints are displayed progressively to avoid spoilers.

T11.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage hints and explanations, including creation, retrieval, and updates.

T12.implementation_approach: Write unit and integration tests to verify the functionality of the problem library.
T12.notes: Test edge cases and error handling.

T13.implementation_approach: Simulate code submissions and evaluate the correctness of the evaluation backend.
T13.notes: Test for security vulnerabilities and performance.

T14.implementation_approach: Test user profile functionalities, including data retrieval and updates.

T15.implementation_approach: Verify the accuracy and performance of the leaderboard functionality.

T16.implementation_approach: Test the functionality of hints and explanations, including progressive hint display.
T16.notes: Ensure hints are displayed in the correct order.

T17.implementation_approach: Deploy the platform using a cloud service provider, ensuring scalability and security.
T17.notes: Set up CI/CD pipelines for automated deployment.

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

# Instantiate SQLAlchemy object
db = SQLAlchemy()

from app.database import db

class Problem(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'problems'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    difficulty = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.now())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, onupdate=db.func.now())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Problem {self.id} - {self.title}>"

from app.database import db

class User(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'users'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    username = db.Column(db.String(80), unique=True, nullable=False)
    email = db.Column(db.String(120), unique=True, nullable=False)
    password_hash = db.Column(db.String(128), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp(), onupdate=db.func.current_timestamp())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<User {self.username}>"

from app.database import db

class Solution(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'solutions'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    problem_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('problems.id'), nullable=False)
    user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('users.id'), nullable=False)
    code = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    language = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, server_default=db.func.now(), nullable=False)
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, server_default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now(), nullable=False)

    def __init__(self, problem_id, user_id, code, language):
        self.problem_id = problem_id
        self.user_id = user_id
        self.code = code
        self.language = language

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<Solution id={self.id} problem_id={self.problem_id} user_id={self.user_id}>'

# app/routes.py

# Required Imports
from app.controllers.problem_controller import problem_blueprint
from app.controllers.user_controller import user_blueprint
from app.controllers.solution_controller import solution_blueprint

def register_blueprints(app):
    """
    Function to register all blueprints with the Flask application instance.

    Parameters:
        app (Flask): The Flask application instance.

    Returns:
        None
    """
    app.register_blueprint(problem_blueprint)
    app.register_blueprint(user_blueprint)
    app.register_blueprint(solution_blueprint)

from flask import Flask
from app.routes import register_blueprints

def create_app():
    """Application factory for the ACM Problem-Solving Platform."""
    app = Flask(__name__)

    # Register routes and blueprints
    register_blueprints(app)

    return app

code_repository.readme_content:
# ACM Problem-Solving Platform

A website designed to help users solve ACM-style programming problems and improve their coding skills.

## Features

- Problem Library: A comprehensive library of ACM-style programming problems categorized by difficulty and topic.
- Code Submission and Evaluation: Allows users to submit code solutions and receive instant feedback on correctness and performance.
- User Profiles: Enables users to create profiles, track their progress, and view their problem-solving history.
- Leaderboard: Displays rankings of users based on their problem-solving performance and achievements.
- Hints and Explanations: Provides hints and detailed explanations for problems to help users learn and improve.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```

## Usage

Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.
